findings.title: Cue is generic, repeated, and does not answer the question asked
findings.expected: A cue he can say to 'Is that dog small too?', such as 'Yes. Biscuit is small.'
findings.got: Same line 'Try: Hi, I am Ali. What is his name?' four times; quiz asked about hello.
findings.evidence: #3-#6 identical cue; #7 'Mrs Lee says hello. What is a good hello back?' while Mrs Lee had asked #2 'Is that dog small too?'
findings.suggested_acceptance: Cue and phrase choice must relate to the partner's current question and change on each press.
findings.code_hint: cue / phrase choice builder, scene-goal-driven fallback

findings.title: No replay with a fresh question after the moment
findings.expected: After the 'small' moment, a new question lets him try the coached word alone.
findings.got: Only 'Back to the conversation'; next question is about having a dog.
findings.evidence: #9 'Back to the conversation'; #10 'Thank you! Do you have a dog?'; #11 still Czech
findings.suggested_acceptance: After a moment, the partner asks a fresh question that uses the coached word.

findings.title: Partner turns drift above A1
findings.expected: One tiny sentence and one simple question with known words.
findings.evidence: #12 'Rex is a nice name! Is Rex a large dog?'; #15 'Is he the same size as Biscuit?'; #16 'fast and strong'
findings.suggested_acceptance: Partner turns for age-9 A1 use one sentence, words from the learner's known set.

findings.title: Moment quotes him exactly and in kid words
findings.evidence: #9 'Small means little in size, not big.'
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep exact quoting and plain Czech-to-English glosses.

findings.title: Situation list long and mixed for a nine-year-old
findings.expected: Short list of play and animal topics.
findings.got: 20 entries incl. booking, lost jacket, group project, speaking practice.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Elementary profile shows only age-fit play and animal situations.

findings.title: Held fixes are redundant and only one was a stop
findings.got: 'Ano' and 'Ano.' held twice with near-identical notes.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Dedupe held fixes by the same word across turns.

findings.title: Supported replies counted honestly
findings.evidence: #17 recap; evidence supported:true for cue turns, false for last two
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep support flag in the progress picture.

judge.voice: Jo, the dog talk was fun, I like Biscuit and Rex. But when I pressed help, it kept saying "Hi, I am Ali. What is his name?" Čtyřikrát! That was not about the small dog, so I just wrote my own thing, half Czech. The "malý is small" bit was nice and easy, and nobody made me feel bad. But then Mrs Lee asked something new, so I never tried "small" again straight away. Some words, like "large" and "same size", I didn't know. At the end I said "Biscuit is small. Rex is big" alone and felt clever. I'd use it again for dogs, but the help must help with the question. Mum would like that it says what I did alone and what with help.

verdictWhy.text: D2 failed: Cue 'Try: Hi, I am Ali. What is his name?' (#3-#6) did not fit 'Is that dog small too?'; quiz #7 asked about 'hello'. His reply #8 was his own Czech mix. The note quoted 'malý' correctly (#9) but came after the reply.
verdictWhy.check: The help actually unblocks the next reply; a coaching note quotes what they really said.

verdictWhy.text: D3 failed: #9 only offers 'Back to the conversation'; #10 'Thank you! Do you have a dog?' is a new topic, not a retry. He answered #11 'Ano. I like dog. Můj pes je Rex.', still Czech.
verdictWhy.check: Replaying the moment gives them a fresh question, and they answer it better than before.
